newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria delays privatisation, says needs study.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria delays privatisation, says needs study.

text.p: Nigeria's military ruler General Sani Abacha said on Saturday his government was interested in privatising state enterprises but needed more consultations to do so effectively.

Abacha, in a nationwide radio and television broadcast of this year's delayed fiscal budget, said the government had over the last few years considered the desirability or otherwise of divesting from public enterprises and would in 1997 undertake a wide range of consultations on the issue.
"Government's interest in the process is to ensure effective and efficient management of these enterprises while the nation gets maximum benefit in terms of services and resources," he said.
"The various options open to government will be closely examined by a high-powered committee before any privatisation exercise is embarked upon," Abacha said.
It was an anti-climax to widespread expectation before the budget that Abacha would announce that privatisation would commence full blast in 1997.

The issue has been at the forefront of discussion in business circles within and outside Nigeria since October when finance minister Anthony Ani announced that Nigeria was seriously considering selling its oil joint ventures and privatising the oil refineries.
Nigeria, sub-Saharan Africa's biggest economy, has been in recession since 1993 when the country slid into crisis over annulment of an election that would have restored democracy.
Free market policies in place since early 1995 have stabilised the economy, and economists say privatisation would have yielded a badly needed injection of funds to stimulate real economic growth.
Ani had argued at a seminar in Lagos that "Privatisation will open our economy up for the foreign investment we very much need."
Abacha said the government would, however, continue with its policy of commercialisation of state enterprises -- encouraging them to operate without subsidies.

"In the entire process, government will take the organised private sector into confidence and will enter into meaningful dialogue with interested foreign partners with whom we can cooperate for the enhancement of our objectives," he said.
